title: infra check and init take one empty NS answer from the machine's resolver as final, and say no authoritative nameserver answered when none was asked -- a transient miss lists a live domain as unmeasured
body:
FOUND 2026-09-24 by prodinfra-cc and sent to vc between their clock's 16:24Z and 16:31Z (vc's date -u read 16:32:16Z). Prodinfra keeps it in its intent/wip.md under "devbin gaps". Filed into 0.1.8 on hv's ruling of 2026-09-24: "Yes, all in 0.1.8, please."

WHAT HAPPENS. infra_dns_authority (lib/infra.dns:65) finds a domain's nameserver with one `dig +short +time=3 +tries=2 NS <fqdn>`. It names no @server, so the question goes to the machine's resolver, and it returns 1 on an empty answer. Both callers take that as final. `infra check` lists the domain under COULD NOT MEASURE with "no authoritative nameserver answered -- NOTHING about this domain was checked" (lib/infra.check:98-101). `infra init` has the domain abstain with "could not be measured: no authoritative nameserver answered for ..." (lib/infra.init:144 and :240). dig's +tries repeats only a query that got no reply. An empty reply is still a reply, whatever its status, and +short drops the status, so neither caller can say what came back.

MEASURED AT PRODINFRA on 2026-09-24: each of six `infra check` runs listed one to three domains as not measured this way. Each of those domains answered SOA and NS at once when asked directly moments later. A run took 7 to 8 s, so these were fast empty answers, not timeouts.

DRIVEN by vc on 2026-09-24 at fe51e3c in a scratch clone. The infra arms' fake dig was extended to log every argv, and to answer the first NS lookup for a domain with nothing and every later one with a nameserver.
- THE CONTROL, every NS lookup answered: "3 assertion(s) held, 0 drift, 0 NOT MEASURED", rc 0.
- ONE EMPTY ANSWER: "0 assertion(s) held, 0 drift, 1 NOT MEASURED", with the domain under COULD NOT MEASURE saying "no authoritative nameserver answered -- NOTHING about this domain was checked", rc 1. The whole run made one dig call, `+short +time=3 +tries=2 NS alpha.example`. No authoritative server was asked anything, and the lookup was never repeated. The next lookup for the same name answered.

NO ARM HOLDS THE TEXT. infra-check.bats:118 (AT-2.3) drives an empty NS answer and asserts "COULD NOT MEASURE" and "NOTHING about this domain was checked", never "no authoritative nameserver answered". infra-init.bats:181 asserts "could not be measured". No arm drives an empty answer that a second lookup would have filled.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO:
- Retry the authority read after a short pause when its answer is empty, a bounded number of times. The domain is not measured only when every attempt came back empty. The pause is a knob beside DEVBIN_INFRA_DNS_TIMEOUT and DEVBIN_INFRA_DNS_TRIES, so an arm can set it to 0.
- Say what was observed: the machine's resolver returned no NS record for the name, on how many attempts, with the status where dig reports one, and no authoritative server was asked. check and init print the same words, from one place.
- Arms: an answer empty once and then filled is measured, not listed, and the dig log shows the second lookup. An answer empty on every attempt is still COULD NOT MEASURE at rc 1, with the new text asserted whole, in check and in init. The existing !NOAUTH arms keep their claims. Red first at fe51e3c, with mutants (no retry, one attempt too few, the old text).
- Pages: lib/pages/infra.md, where it says what COULD NOT MEASURE means for the authority read.

The exit code is not this issue's: 0126 (closed 2026-09-23) already makes it 1 in 0.1.8. This changes when a domain lands in COULD NOT MEASURE and what it says there. vc's. It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling.

## Resolution

Fixed at 5ea1905. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. In lib/infra.dns, the one reader check and init share: when the NS answer holds no NS record, the question is asked again after DEVBIN_INFRA_DNS_RETRY_PAUSE seconds (default 1, from RFC 9520's minimum SERVFAIL cache), up to three attempts, and the domain is unmeasured only when every attempt came back without one. A query dig could not complete (exit 9) or could not run is not asked again. _idns_ask is the one dig invocation and owns the flags the parsers depend on; the status and rows are read for both readers, rows filtered by type, so a CNAME row is never taken as the nameserver, and the pick takes the sorted first. infra_dns_no_authority builds one sentence, printed by check and recorded by init: what each attempt got, in order, and that devbin asked no authoritative nameserver, which is what it did. The three knobs are validated once per run, a whole number below 100000, refused at exit 1 before anything is measured. The fake dig, the fake sleep and `zone` are one strict fake in tests/lib/infra_fakes.bash, which accepts exactly the argv lib/infra.dns sends. And a leak devbin-cc found: infra.bats and infra-dmarc-report.bats gained teardown(), and a contract.bats tree scan holds that every suite calling devbin_setup has one.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. An empty NOERROR or an NXDOMAIN is a negative answer a resolver caches for the zone's negative TTL, so raising the pause will not help there; the page says so, and says which status it can help with. The exit codes are 0126's.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell reviewed the code and checked the arms; its code findings (MX1 to MX5) and test findings (SV1 to SV9) were built and each became a mutant. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-25, approved at v2 on the patch, the fake's strictness, the drive with the real dig and the evidence below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. The two infra files on 2b46d85's lib under DIG_LEGACY=1: 15 of 59 red, the 14 arms asserting what 0142 changes, each for its own reason, and the fake's own control; the five arms guarding behaviour already true there each run red against the mutant it exists to kill; the teardown scan red on the tree before the two teardowns, naming exactly those two suites. 48 mutants, each against the arms it aims at: 48 of 48 killed.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the nine 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on b10dd41 (0139, 0128, 0133, 0130, 0142, 0143, 0144, 0146, 0147), on a clean checkout (head 308cf21), 2026-09-25 11:34:20Z to 12:09:20Z: 1907 of 1907 ok, 0 not ok, no gaps, its 5 skips the suite's declared ones. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree outside intent/.
